system: mixed system of Islamic (sharia) law and civil law

constitution.history: previous 1971 (provisional); latest drafted in 1979, became permanent May 1996
constitution.amend: proposed by the Supreme Council and submitted to the Federal National Council; passage requires at least a two-thirds majority vote of Federal National Council members present and approval of the Supreme Council president

courts.highest: Federal Supreme Court (consists of the court president and 4 judges; jurisdiction limited to federal cases)
courts.judges: judges appointed by the federal president after approval from the Federal Supreme Council, the highest executive and legislative authority consisting of the 7 emirate rulers; judges serve until retirement age or the expiration of their appointment terms
courts.lower: Federal Court of Cassation (determines the constitutionality of laws); the emirates of Abu Dhabi, Dubai, and Ra's al Khaymah have parallel court systems; the other 4 emirates have incorporated their courts into the federal system
courts.note: the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts and the Dubai International Financial Center Courts, the country’s two largest financial free zones, adjudicate civil and commercial disputes

citizenship.descent: the father must be a citizen of the United Arab Emirates; if the father is unknown, the mother must be a citizen

world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; non-party state to the ICCt
